paragraphs.text: Zinny the Zebra reared up on her back legs. Then she dropped down on her back. Dirt flew up as she rolled on the ground.
"What on earth?" yelled Ollie the Oxpecker. He flew up in a cloud of dust and feathers. "You almost fell on me!"
Zinny quickly stood up and said, "I'm sorry! I didn't mean to scare you. I just wanted to scratch my back."
Ollie calmed down. "Well, no harm done," he said. "But you can't just keep crashing around on the ground."
"How else can I get rid of these bugs?" Zinny asked.
"Wait," said Ollie. "Bugs? That's what's making you itch?"
Zinny nodded.
Ollie grinned. "I believe I can help with that problem." Flying up onto Zinny's back, he started picking off the bugs and eating them.
"Oh, thank you," Zinny said. "That feels so much better! Is there anything I can do for you?"
Ollie stopped snacking for a moment. "You're already doing it," he said. "I've got a yummy meal and a great place to sit!"

paragraphs.text: Lucas and Dad waited outside for Aunt Sandy. "I wish you could come with us," Lucas said to Dad.
"Me too. I'd love to visit Animal Friends," Dad said. Animal Friends was where Aunt Sandy worked. Pets without homes lived there until they found families.
The neighbor's cat trotted over. "No, Coco," Dad said. But it was too late. Dad started to sneeze.
Lucas carried Coco back to the neighbor's yard. Coco purred in his arms, and he sighed. Lucas wanted a pet, but furry animals made Dad feel sick.
"Aunt Sandy is here!" Dad called. Lucas ran to Aunt Sandy's car. At least he could have fun at Animal Friends. Poor Dad couldn't even do that.
And Lucas did have fun. He got to walk all the dogs. Then Aunt Sandy asked, "Want to see the pig?"
"The pig?"
"Yep. His name is Marvin. Pot-bellied pigs make good pets."
Lucas was surprised by how friendly Marvin was. "Hey!" Lucas said. "He has no fur!"
Aunt Sandy said, "Are you thinking what I'm thinking?"
Lucas almost danced with excitement. "Marvin won't make Dad sick! He's the perfect pet!"

Finn nodded. The tree was so big that Finn couldn't even see the top.
The tree was easy to climb, though. And as the boys climbed, the branches got wider and wider.

Lucy ran to the kitchen.
A big stuffed giraffe was sitting in her chair. Lucy laughed.
Someone else laughed, too. It was Aunt Maddie! "Happy Birthday, Lucy!" Aunt Maddie said. "Guess where we're going today!"
"The best place in the world!" Lucy said, jumping up and down.
"Yep," said Aunt Maddie.
After breakfast, Aunt Maddie and Lucy got in the car. Soon, they arrived at the best place in the world. The zoo!

paragraphs.text: Mia waved to Mom and swam off to find the giant sea worms. There were a lot of great things about living in a science station under the ocean. But the sea worms were the best part.
Mia just needed to remember not to touch them. Never, ever. The worms were covered with sticky slime. It was like glue!
Mia spotted Gerty near the station's main air tube. Of all the sea worms, Mia liked Gerty best. Mia swam toward Gerty.
But what was that?
Air bubbles were floating from the air tube! Mia looked closely at the tube. Sure enough, there was a small leak.
This was not good. If the leak got worse, the station could run out of air.
An idea popped into Mia's head. She pulled a treat from her bag. Gerty smiled and came closer. Mia held the treat near the tube, just above the leak. As Gerty took it, she brushed against the tube.
The goo from Gerty's skin covered up the hole. The bubbles stopped.
"Whew! You saved the day, Gerty!" Mia said. "And the air!"

Paul waved his hand. "Probably a bear."
"Bears are in their dens for the winter," Dana replied.
Paul rolled his eyes, but Dana knew she was right. Bears were sleeping now.
After breakfast, Dana filled a basket with food. She pulled on snow pants, a jacket, and boots. Then, she walked into the forest and left the food by an old log.
The next morning, Dana returned to the log. The food was gone, and there were fresh footprints! They were large, like the ones Dana had seen before.
Then, Dana saw something else. It was a small pile of pine branches, bright green against the snow. Someone had bent them into a heart shape.
Gently, Dana touched the heart. It didn't matter what Paul thought. Bigfoot was real.

"Two beautiful kittens," Kiara finally whispered.
"One for each of us," Tiara whispered back.
